subject: Clarify storage responsibility & SOC 2 evidence for Zenovia
messages:
From: Aria Patel <aria.patel@zenoviahealth.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: security@zenoviahealth.com
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 09:13:00 -0700
Subject: Request: S3 backups + SOC 2 coverage for subservice mapping

Hi Vivek,

Hope you're well — we're onboarding Redwood as a subservice and our audit team has a couple of items to close out for our SOC 2 mapping. Can you confirm the following?

1) Do Redwood backups of customer data to S3 fall under Redwood's responsibility in scope for SOC 2 Type II, or are they considered an AWS-managed carve-out? We need explicit language for our artifact mapping.

2) Can you provide your latest SOC 2 Type II report and, if applicable, a bridge letter that explains the carve-out boundary for AWS services and the audit window (we're looking to cover Sep 01, 2026 — Aug 31, 2027 in our inventory).

3) For evidence, our team typically asks for: subprocessors list, S3 lifecycle/backup policy, KMS key management evidence, and confirmation of cross-region replication (if any). If you can point to which artifacts you can provide, or templates we should expect, that would help us prioritize.

We're trying to lock this for our compliance run next week. If easier, happy to do a quick call — looping in our security lead, Carl Nguyen (cc).

Thanks,
Aria Patel
Head of Security Operations
Zenovia Health

[signature block]
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwoodinference.com>
To: Aria Patel <aria.patel@zenoviahealth.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwoodinference.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: S3 backups + SOC 2 coverage for subservice mapping

Hi Aria — thanks for the clear list. Quick answers up front, then details below:

- Attached: our latest SOC 2 Type II report (redwood_soc2_type2_2026.pdf) and current subprocessors list.
- Bridge letter: we can produce a tailored bridge letter that explicitly states how AWS-managed controls (e.g., physical infrastructure, hypervisor) are carved out and which storage-specific AWS responsibilities are expected. We'll draft that and share by EOD tomorrow.
- S3 backups: Redwood initiates and manages customer backups to an S3 bucket that we control within the customer partition; operational controls around backup jobs, lifecycle policies, and encryption-at-rest are Redwood responsibilities. However, AWS is responsible for the underlying fabric (physical security, host OS). For SOC 2 mapping, this typically shows as a shared responsibility: Redwood controls application-level encryption, access controls, and backup scheduling; AWS controls infrastructure availability and host protections.

Evidence we can provide immediately:
- redwood_soc2_type2_2026.pdf (attached)
- redwood_subprocessors_list_2027.csv (attached)
- export of S3 lifecycle/replication policy (s3_lifecycle_policy_export.txt)
- KMS key rotation summary and a link to key material (we'll extract a time-windowed log)

Open items for us to confirm:
- Whether Zenovia requires explicit documentation that cross-region replication (if enabled) is part of Redwood's operational scope. We currently enable cross-region replication only when configured by the customer — if Zenovia has it turned on, we can provide replication job metadata.
- Audit window wording: you asked for Sep 01, 2026 — Aug 31, 2027; we need to confirm that the bridge letter references Redwood's internal audit period versus AWS artifact coverage. I'll coordinate with Priyom on language.

I'll attach the SOC report and subprocessors list now. Priyom / Mina — could you take point on the bridge-letter draft and KMS log extract?

Best,
Vivek Kulkarni
Director, Trust & Safety
Redwood Inference

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwoodinference.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwoodinference.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 23 Apr 2027 09:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: S3 backups + SOC 2 coverage for subservice mapping

Vivek / Mina — adding internal notes and proposed artifact list to attach with the bridge letter. Forwarding Vivek's response below for context.

On Thu, Apr 22, 2027 at 10:05 AM Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwoodinference.com> wrote:
> (see message above)

Proposed bundle for Zenovia:
- Finalized bridge letter (customized: call out "AWS shared-responsibility: compute/physical/hypervisor carve-out; Redwood controls: backup scheduling, object lifecycle, encryption keys, access controls"). Use plain language and include the audit window.
- Excerpt from AWS SOC report referencing S3 services (we can link to the AWS artifact where allowed).
- S3 lifecycle policy export (s3_lifecycle_policy_export.txt).
- KMS key management evidence: rotation schedule + sample key event log (we will redact per privacy).
- Subprocessor list (redwood_subprocessors_list_2027.csv) — highlight any third-party backup services if used (none for Zenovia unless enabled).
- Optional: architecture diagram showing where backups are written and which VPC/subnet they reside in (we'll generate a lightweight PNG).

A couple of clarifying Qs before we finalize:
1) Does Zenovia need the bridge letter to state specific AWS report dates (e.g., "AWS SOC 2 Type II report covering Jan‑Dec 2026") or is a general statement about AWS responsibility enough?
2) Does the compliance team need evidence of any tenant-level configuration we performed (e.g., IAM roles used for backup jobs)? If so, we should include an audited IAM role change log slice.

I'll prepare the bridge_letter_draft_for_zenovia.docx and the KMS log slice by tomorrow. Mina — can you pull a sanitized IAM role activity log and the diagram?

Thanks,
Priyom
Sr. Compliance Manager
Redwood Inference

Thanks Vivek and team — this is very helpful. A couple quick follow-ups:

- Replication: Zenovia does use cross-region replication for our backups; please include the replication job metadata in the bundle if possible. That will show whether replication jobs are initiated by Redwood or by Zenovia config.
- AWS report citation: please include the explicit AWS SOC 2 report date range in the bridge letter if you can (we need to reference it in our inventory).
- Audit confirmation: can you confirm the date of Redwood's latest audit? The SOC 2 attached looks like it covers calendar year 2026; we just need a one-line confirmation for our tracker.

If you can send the draft bridge letter and the KMS log slice today, we can route to audit for a quick review.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Regards,
Aria Patel
Head of Security Operations
Zenovia Health
